description: The AAO filter set catalogs optical broad-band and narrow-band filters historically offered for CCD direct imaging and focal plane instruments at the Anglo-Australian Telescope (AAT).
short_description: Anglo-Australian Telescope broad- and narrow-band filters (AAO)
facility_description: The Anglo-Australian Telescope (AAT) is a 3.9-meter equatorially mounted optical telescope at Siding Spring Observatory in New South Wales, operated by the Australian National University (ANU).
notes: AAO filters originate from the AAO Master Filter Catalog for the 3.9m Anglo-Australian Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory. Operation of the AAT was transferred to the Australian National University (ANU). Terms follow ANU website copyright policy restricting reproduction without permission. DetectorType of aao62, aao63 set to photon, DetectorTypeSource inferred (2026-11-11), the label every served copy of the same curve now carries: ING's filter database gives this curve as 'ING Filter Throughput Data' of the filter alone, in percent, scanned on 2005-03-02 (catserver.ing.iac.es/filter/filtercurve.php, archived 2010; https://astro.ing.iac.es/filter/). The AAO Master Filter Catalog lists the same TAURUS filters (AAO #62 'WHT Filter f126', #63 'WHT Filter f107') with the same data. They are TAURUS filters (ING passbands 'TAURUS 5220/380' and 'TAURUS 5000/350'), for the TAURUS-2 focal reducer at the WHT and AAT, read by CCDs (Bland-Hawthorn & Jones 1998, PASA 15, 44). A filter-only transmission used with a CCD counts photons. SVO's DetectorType is not used.
